criteria.text: A scheduled task with no allowed_mcps_json, bound to a profile scoped to ["rhythm"], runs with exactly the rhythm tools and cannot call out-of-scope tools (scheduler passes undefined so the runner inherits the profile scope).
criteria.test_id: scope-c1: task with null allowed_mcps_json → run() receives allowedMcpsJson: undefined (inherit)

criteria.text: Changing the profile's allowed_mcps_json changes what the task can do on its next run, with NO edit to the task (scope is resolved live).
criteria.test_id: scope-c2: editing the profile changes the resolved MCP scope on the next call (no override)

criteria.text: A task WITH an explicit allowlist still overrides the profile.
criteria.test_id: scope-c3: task with explicit allowed_mcps_json → run() receives that value (override)

criteria.text: The same inheritance/override precedence applies to allowed_skills_json (skills filtering), not just MCPs.
criteria.test_id: scope-c4: allowedSkillsJsonOverride takes precedence over the profile allowed_skills_json

criteria.text: The create-task path (MCP tool + REST) does NOT require an allowlist — omitting it means "inherit from profile".
criteria.test_id: scope-c5: does NOT require allowedMcps/allowedSkills (omitting = inherit)

criteria.text: At dispatch the scheduler forwards the task's own allowed_skills_json as a skills override when set, and undefined (inherit) when null/empty.
criteria.test_id: scope-c6: task with explicit allowed_skills_json → run() receives that value
